assessment_summary.cou_name: Predict hottest module temperature and coolant rise for M5 cold plate to support EVT

evidence_keywords: Ansys Fluent 2023R2
Traceability: Inputs and case files for R03–R10 are on Git (tag m5_cht_ev1).
Peer read by S. Ng
Double precision throughout except R06
Verified pressure drop against a straight-channel correlation (turbulent) and got within 4%.
pipe-heating sanity case from White (convective heat-up) and got 0.3% error
relevance to our strongly 3D corner flows is limited.
Mesh sensitivity: Across 5.2M → 14.7M, hottest-cap prediction shifted 1.2%.
monotonicity assumption behind the GCI we quoted (0.5%) is shaky.
Near-wall target was y+≈1
Convergence: Energy residuals <1e-6, others <1e-4.
flattened to within 0.2 C
in R08 the hottest node drifted ~0.8 C
single precision to test speed
Run R09 included surface-to-surface radiation by mistake
R01–R02 inadvertently used a fixed viscosity μ=1.5e-3 Pa·s
bookkeeping issues
we started with 5% (legacy template) and used 10% in later runs
SST k-ω for the coolant with curvature correction off.
Radiation: off in the baseline
board modeled as orthotropic equivalent (kxx=12, kyy=12, kzz=0.8 W/m-K).
We’ve treated the solution as steady.
50/50 water–glycol loop, nominal 2.0 L/min at 25 C inlet
Vendor sheet lists turbulence intensity ≈10%
Loads: 180 W total, apportioned 45/45/45/45 W
TIM-1 between die caps and spreader, nominal 0.10 mm thickness; TIM-2 under spreader to plate, 0.08 mm nominal.
Temperature-dependent coolant properties via NIST tables
M5 coupon on the thermal stand
T-type microbead in each module cap
IR spot check through the window
2.0 L/min, 25 C inlet, 180 W.
Hottest cap measured 68.5±0.7 C
coolant rise 3.6±0.2 C.
Lock inlet turbulence intensity to 10% to match the pump data
Remove radiation entirely for the sealed-enclosure condition
Calibrate thermal interfaces using the metrology thickness distribution rather than a single nominal
Baseline steady run (R07) predicted 63.2 C hottest cap and 3.2 C coolant rise.
Hottest cap measured 68.5±0.7 C; coolant rise 3.6±0.2 C.
That’s ~8% low on peak temperature.
we called this “within 3%” using R05
